note: These are runtime design tensions, not new scientific edges. A conflict fires only when its participants are active in the current case.

conflicts.name: Norm pressure vs autonomy/reactance
conflicts.resolution: Prefer autonomy-supportive wording, descriptive evidence, or value relevance over controlling 'you should' language when reactance is active.

conflicts.name: Proof detail vs processing burden
conflicts.resolution: Layer proof: surface the most diagnostic evidence first; make depth available without forcing all detail into the first exposure.

conflicts.name: Complexity vs fluency
conflicts.resolution: Resolve avoidable ambiguity; retain complexity only when it carries necessary precision or meaning.

conflicts.name: Comparative contrast vs credibility
conflicts.resolution: Use factual, symmetric comparison criteria and support claims; avoid exaggerated superiority that creates trust costs.

conflicts.name: Emotion intensity vs decision risk
conflicts.resolution: Use emotion to make stakes relevant, but pair high-risk decisions with evidence/control information rather than escalating affect alone.

conflicts.name: Action directness vs reactance
conflicts.resolution: Keep next action clear while preserving choice/autonomy and avoiding coercive pressure.

conflicts.name: Narrative depth vs action clarity
conflicts.resolution: Use narrative only as long as it supports value/belief change; make the transition to next action explicit and low-friction.

conflicts.name: Specificity vs unsupported precision
conflicts.resolution: Be specific where facts are verifiable; do not invent precise numbers/claims to create credibility.
